pairs.subject: invariant-placement
pairs.evidence: packages/domain/src/project.ts:57 The domain names each rule's altitude: structural rules sit at zod doors (plan graph, slot field/state coupling), states are derived instead of stored, and exhaustive keyed tables make a new op or kind fail to compile. Negative tests check that the doors refuse bad input.

techniques.evidence: packages/domain/src/project.ts:57 The altitude is named in the code: cycles and dangling edges are refused at the door when the plan is written, so they are never discovered mid-run.
packages/domain/src/project.ts:11 projectSchema has no state field. State is computed from the parts (projectStateOf), and part state comes from job and packet the same way (part.ts:9).
packages/domain/src/partView.ts:281 A mapped type keyed by the op union, so an op added without an entry here is a type error. opLabel's switch also has no default arm.
packages/domain/src/partView.ts:48 Two hand-maintained tables (the editor kinds and the catalogue's work kinds) are checked against each other at compile time with `satisfies`.
packages/domain/src/partView.ts:140 The view contract leaves out absent optional parts instead of defaulting them. PartView's mapped type requires a data field for every editor kind.

packages/domain/src/slot.machine.ts:16 The encoding gives at-most-once, and the comment next to it says it does not give at-least-once: a dead holder leaves the slot `publishing`, the sweep marks it failed, and a person reschedules it.

packages/domain/test/project.test.ts:39 Each rule raised to the door has a negative test. The refuse() helper asserts the stable code `invalid` plus a fragment of the project's own message (not toolchain text), so the dependence on wording is only partial.
packages/domain/src/part.ts:58 Ids get a separate brand per record (ids.ts idSchema("PartId") etc.), applied at the producing door, so a JobId and a PartId cannot be swapped.
packages/domain/src/partView.ts:65 The resolver signals 'no face' with null in a wrapper; ResearchFace gains no none-of-these member.
packages/domain/src/slot.ts:83 The doors refuse and never repair. A grep of the context files for .catch(/.default(/.transform(/.preprocess( found nothing.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/library/_port/present.ts:59 This is a total fold over an owned closed union with a default arm instead of an exhaustive switch. Adding a member to LIBRARY_KINDS does not stop the build here.
app/(studio)/library/_port/actions.ts:28 An out-of-range page limit is refused at the zod door, not clamped.
app/(studio)/library/_port/actions.ts:5 Input rules are placed at one construction door per action (runAction/action), not checked at call sites in the sides.
app/(studio)/library/_port/present.ts:129 `pinned` is computed from the acts the index offers, not stored or declared beside them.
app/(studio)/library/_port/present.ts:133 The one mapping that both sides emit through leaves out absent optional parts instead of defaulting them.

pairs.registryProposal: a-new-field-must-choose could say how it applies to TypeScript if-chains that narrow a union and end in a fallthrough return. That is the common TS form of a default arm, and the technique currently names only match/switch default arms.
